title: Folded Cascode
intro: The cascode device need not be the same type as the input device. Steering the input current into a cascode device of the opposite type folds the signal path, which frees headroom at the cost of extra bias current (Razavi, Section 3.6.1).

blocks.text: A cascode converts the input voltage to a current and hands it to a common-gate device. A PMOS input device can hand its current to an NMOS CG device just as well. The PMOS M1 and NMOS M2 then need a separate bias current $I_1$ at the folding node X: $|I_{D1}| + I_{D2} = I_1$. If $V_{in}$ rises, $|I_{D1}|$ falls, so $I_{D2}$ rises by the same amount and the output drops. The mirror-image version uses an NMOS input and a PMOS cascode device. The small-signal gain and output resistance are found exactly as for the telescopic cascode.

blocks.alt: Two folded cascode stages. (a) PMOS M1 from VDD to node X, gate driven by Vin; NMOS M2 with gate at Vb has its source at X and its drain at the output, which connects to VDD through RD; current source I1 from X to ground. (b) Current source I1 from VDD into node X; NMOS M1 from X to ground with gate driven by Vin; PMOS M2 with gate at Vb has its source at X and drain at the output, which connects to ground through RD.
blocks.caption: Folded cascodes: (a) PMOS input with NMOS cascode, the current folded up; (b) NMOS input with PMOS cascode, the current folded down.

blocks.text: In a telescopic cascode the same bias current flows through the input and cascode devices: it is reused. In a folded cascode the two branches each need their own current, both supplied from $I_1$, so for comparable performance the folded stage draws more current (often about twice). In return the input and output no longer sit in one stack, which eases the headroom and input-range limits; that is why folded cascodes are common op amp input stages (see Operational Amplifiers).
In version (a), sweep $V_{in}$ down from $V_{DD}$. Above $V_{DD} - |V_{TH1}|$, M1 is off, M2 carries all of $I_1$ and $V_{out} = V_{DD} - I_1R_D$. Below it, M1 turns on in saturation and
so $V_{out}$ rises as $V_{in}$ falls. $I_{D2}$ reaches zero when M1 alone carries $I_1$, at

Below $V_{in1}$, M1 would like to carry more than $I_1$ and is pushed into triode instead. Meanwhile node X rises as $I_{D2}$ falls, reaching $V_b - V_{TH2}$ when M2 turns off, and heads toward $V_{DD}$ once M1 is in triode. (If $I_1$ is too large, M2 and the current source itself can be driven into triode.)
With the bias current source implemented by a transistor M3, the cascode device M2 is degenerated by $r_{o1} \parallel r_{o3}$ instead of $r_{o1}$:

It is lower than the telescopic cascode's because of the extra $r_{o3}$ at the folding node. For high gain the load is itself made a cascode current source; this structure is developed as the folded-cascode op amp.

items: Telescopic: highest gain and output resistance for a given current, lowest power and noise, but the smallest output swing and a limited input common-mode range, since everything is in one stack.

Folded: more swing and input range (the input level can be near a rail), at the cost of extra bias current, somewhat lower output resistance, and the noise and capacitance of the extra device at the folding node.

blocks.text: A very high output resistance makes the output node slow when it drives a capacitance, but inside a feedback loop this is not the problem it seems (see Feedback and Stability and Frequency Compensation).

blocks.title: Folded versus telescopic output resistance
blocks.text: $g_{m2} = 1\text{ mS}$, $g_{mb2} = 0.2\text{ mS}$, $r_{o1} = r_{o2} = 40\text{ k}\Omega$ and the folding current source has $r_{o3} = 20\text{ k}\Omega$. Find $R_{out}$ of the folded cascode and of a telescopic cascode with the same M1 and M2.
solution: $(g_{m2} + g_{mb2})r_{o2} = 48$. Folded: $r_{o1} \parallel r_{o3} = 13.3\text{ k}\Omega$, so $R_{out} = 49 \cdot 13.3 + 40 \approx 693\text{ k}\Omega$.
Telescopic: $49 \cdot 40 + 40 = 2000\text{ k}\Omega = 2\text{ M}\Omega$, about three times higher.

blocks.title: Where the cascode branch turns off
blocks.text: In version (a), $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_1 = 200\,\mu\text{A}$, $\mu_p C_{ox}(W/L)_1 = 1\text{ mA/V}^2$ and $|V_{TH1}| = 0.45\text{ V}$. At what input does $I_{D2}$ reach zero, and at what input do M1 and M2 carry equal currents?
blocks.answer: $V_{in1} \approx 0.72\text{ V}$; equal currents at about 0.90 V.

blocks.title: Current budget
blocks.text: A telescopic cascode runs at $100\,\mu\text{A}$. A folded cascode must give the input device and the cascode device $100\,\mu\text{A}$ each at the operating point. What must $I_1$ be, and how does total supply current compare?
solution: At the operating point $I_1 = |I_{D1}| + I_{D2} = 200\,\mu\text{A}$, and all of it comes from the supply (in version (a) M1's current and RD's current both come from VDD and leave through $I_1$).
